# Brief for EDGE

Focus: robustness, deployability and sovereignty. Project: Taadeel (تعديل), a research and navigation tool for amendments to UAE federal legislation. It is not legal advice. The official Arabic text published by the competent authority prevails.

## Problem

A tool that tracks changes to legislation may be read as authoritative whether or not it claims to be. It has to be deployable in a controlled environment, make no calls to outside services at run time, keep a verifiable record of every source it used, and fail visibly. Four risks matter: poisoned source text, tampering with stored snapshots, overclaiming (synthetic or foreign data shown as UAE law), and loss of availability when a source blocks access. Data residency belongs to the owner of the data, not to the developer.

## What exists

* **Container.** A Docker image (Python slim base) holds the code, the web page and a small UK validation corpus. It makes no external calls at run time and starts with one command. `/api/health` is the health check.
* **Demo host.** A live demo runs on the Render free tier (region chosen in the hosting dashboard, not in `render.yaml`). This is not sovereign hosting. It exists to show behaviour, not to hold data that matters.
* **Residency.** A sovereign deployment would run the same image on UAE hosted infrastructure. The choice of host is to be decided by the owner of the data. Nothing in the project assumes a particular provider.
* **Provenance and integrity.** Every stored expression carries its source URL, retrieval time and a sha256 content hash. UK fetches are logged in a manifest with hashes. The ingestion adapter refuses any host not marked as permitted, reads robots.txt first, treats an unreadable robots.txt as a refusal, and stops on a block.
* **Labels and schema checks.** The store enforces, with database constraints, that a record is synthetic if and only if it sits in the synthetic corpus and carries the synthetic prefix. Real views never include synthetic records. The web page shows a distinct badge for synthetic, UK validation and real data.
* **Hash locked evidence.** Engine files are recorded by sha256 in the result files. Evaluations are pre registered, run once, and refuse a second run.
* **Akoma Ntoso export.** An Akoma Ntoso compatible export, checked against the OASIS Akoma Ntoso 1.0 schema (`akomantoso30.xsd`). The claim is compatible, not compliant: no lifecycle events, no modification elements, and URIs that are the project's own.

## Measured evidence

Scope is stated on each line. None of it concerns UAE law.

* **Export validity, synthetic and UK exports.** {akn_valid} of {akn_total} exported documents validate against the schema, and {akn_controls} of {akn_controls_total} deliberately broken negative controls are rejected. This checks structure only, not meaning.
* **Failure surfaced instead of hidden, UK English.** Where recorded effects omit a change date, the point in time answer is marked uncertain. Of {tl_queries} day before queries, the effects only method served the wrong text on {tl_old_wrong}. The snapshot aware method answered certain and wrong on {tl_certain_wrong}, certain and correct on {tl_certain_correct}, and uncertain on {tl_uncertain}. In {tl_uncertain_hit} of the uncertain answers the true text was among the candidates. The method is served by `/api/timeline` for the UK validation corpus from precomputed steps, so a request runs no alignment and no network call.
* **Invisible character handling, synthetic Arabic.** A set of {ar_cases} invented Arabic strings includes invisible format characters. The locked v1 normaliser passes {ar_v1_ok}; the v2 pre clean passes {ar_v2_ok}, by construction because it was written after seeing the cases. It is not yet wired into the parser or the store.

## Threat model and failure modes

| risk | control in place | status |
|---|---|---|
| Data poisoning from a source | source URL, retrieval date and content hash on every record; text shown beside a link to the official source | detection after the fact, not prevention |
| Hidden characters in source text | normalisation v2 removes bidirectional and zero width characters in the matching copy | tested on synthetic strings only, not wired in |
| Tampering with snapshots | content hashes; derived data regenerated from result files | hashes are not signed |
| Overclaiming | labels on every response; not legal advice banner; unvalidated status stated | in place |
| Synthetic data leaking into real views | schema constraints in the store | in place |
| Portal blocks access | the adapter stops, records the block, and does not work around it | observed: HTTP 403 on robots.txt |
| Effect without a date | the point in time answer is uncertain, with candidates | measured on UK data above |
| Availability | single container, no external dependency at run time | free tier host sleeps when idle |

## What is NOT validated

* Nothing is validated on UAE law or on real Arabic legal text. No real UAE law is loaded. A permission request is drafted and has not been sent.
* UK numbers say nothing about UAE law. Schedules are excluded from the UK evaluation. Hand checks were done by the author, not by a lawyer.
* No penetration test, load test or independent security review has been done. Hashes detect change but do not prove authenticity of the source.
* Akoma Ntoso compatibility is structural only. Resource sizing for a larger corpus is not measured.

## Ask

* A target environment description (operating system, network policy, container runtime) so the image can be tested against it.
* A reviewer for the threat model and the hosting decision, who can state what residency the owner of the data requires.
* Optionally, a sandbox in which to run the container with outbound traffic blocked, to confirm the no external calls property.

## Three month plan

* Month 1: write the threat model as a checked document with an owner for each risk, and add a test that fails if the container opens an outbound connection. Exit check: the test runs in the build and passes with outbound traffic blocked.
* Month 2: sign and verify snapshot manifests, and add a restore from manifest check. Exit check: a tampered snapshot is detected by a command that exits non zero, shown on a synthetic example.
* Month 3: deploy the image in the target environment supplied, and record a load and failure test. Exit check: a written report with the measured results, regenerated by `python -m taadeel.report`, and every limit stated.
